title: Professional Email: Microsoft 365 Organisation Seat Total
content:
All of a customer's Microsoft 365 subscriptions belong to one Microsoft 365 organisation, so their Business seats are counted together. In Professional Email an order, a seat addition or a renewal seat count on a Microsoft 365 Business product may be accepted only when the customer's Microsoft 365 seat total after the change does not exceed the most seats the Microsoft 365 Business products allow per subscription. Harborline Mail subscriptions are counted per subscription against their own seat maximum and never toward the Microsoft 365 total.

## How the Microsoft 365 seat total is counted

The total is the sum of the seat counts on the customer's subscriptions whose product is Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Microsoft 365 Business Standard or Microsoft 365 Business Premium and whose status is provisioning, active, suspended, cancel pending or expired. It is read from the customer's current subscription records.

| Change | Accepted only when |
|---|---|
| New Microsoft 365 Business order | the total including the new seats does not exceed the Microsoft 365 Business seat maximum |
| Seats added to a Microsoft 365 Business subscription | the total after the addition does not exceed it |
| Seat count for a Microsoft 365 Business renewal | the total with the renewal seat count does not exceed it |

## Worked example (hypothetical portfolio)

A customer holds a Microsoft 365 Business Basic subscription with 40 seats in status active, a Microsoft 365 Business Standard subscription with 25 seats in status expired, and a Harborline Mail Pro subscription with 90 seats. The Microsoft 365 total is 40 plus 25, that is 65 seats; the 90 Harborline Mail Pro seats are not counted. With the Microsoft 365 Business maximum of 300 seats, a request to add 10 seats to the Basic subscription is accepted (75 seats), while a request to add 250 seats is refused (315 seats).
